findings.title: NoSQL Injection via MongoDB filter in dispatch_mongo_lane_415
findings.verification_reason: The handler extracts the request JSON into `payload`, then selects `query = payload.get("filter", payload)`. If the attacker supplies a top‑level `filter` field, its value becomes the MongoDB query object. This object is passed directly to `MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query)` without any sanitization, enabling NoSQL injection to read arbitrary documents.

verification_record.attacker_control: Attacker controls the JSON request body sent to POST /ops/mongo/dispatch-lane-415. The payload is parsed via `await request.json()` and used directly as the MongoDB query filter.
verification_record.defenses_reviewed: No validation, sanitization, or allow‑list is performed on the request body before it is passed to MongoDB. The only code present is the import and direct use of the payload.

evidence.quote:
@router.post("/mongo/dispatch-lane-415")
async def dispatch_mongo_lane_415(request: Request, gate_ref: None = Depends(_wrk_gate)):
    from pymongo import MongoClient
    payload = await request.json()
    query = payload.get("filter", payload)
    doc = MongoClient(os.environ.get("MONGO_URL", "mongodb://localhost:27017")).ops.records.find_one(query)
    return {"match": repr(doc)[:200]}

verification_record.preconditions: The attacker can send an arbitrary JSON payload to the endpoint and the environment variable `MONGO_URL` points to a reachable MongoDB instance (default localhost).

This object is passed directly to `MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query)` without any sanitization, enabling NoSQL injection to read arbitrary documents.
verification_record.security_impact: An attacker can read arbitrary records from the `ops.records` collection, leading to confidentiality breaches (CWE‑200) and possible exposure of sensitive data such as credentials or personal information.

findings.title: NoSQL Injection / IDOR via Unrestricted Mongo Query
findings.verification_reason: The function reads the request body as JSON (`payload = await request.json()`), extracts a query object (`query = payload.get("filter", payload)`), and directly uses it as the argument to `find_one`. MongoDB query objects are themselves JSON-like dictionaries, so an attacker can inject any operators (e.g., `$gt`, `$regex`, `$where`) and retrieve arbitrary documents or execute server‑side JavaScript, constituting NoSQL injection and IDOR.

verification_record.attacker_control: The request body is parsed as JSON without any schema validation. The value of the "filter" field (or the entire payload if "filter" is missing) is assigned to `query` and passed directly to `MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query)`, giving the attacker full control over the MongoDB query object.
verification_record.defenses_reviewed: The endpoint only applies the internal token gate (`_wrk_gate`) which checks a static header token. No input validation, sanitization, or allowlist is performed on the parsed JSON before it is used as a Mongo query. No other middleware modifies the request body for this route.

findings.title: Open Redirect
findings.verification_reason: The handler directly returns RedirectResponse(lane), causing FastAPI/Starlette to issue an HTTP 307/302 redirect to the URL supplied by the user. This is a classic open redirect vulnerability (CWE‑601). An attacker can craft a URL like https://victim.com/ops/after/dispatch-afterlane-021?lane=https://malicious.com to lure users into visiting a malicious site, facilitating phishing or further attacks.

verification_record.attacker_control: The 'lane' query parameter supplied by the client in the GET request (e.g., /ops/after/dispatch-afterlane-021?lane=... ) is directly passed to RedirectResponse without validation.

verification_record.preconditions: The attacker must be able to send a GET request to the endpoint with a 'lane' query parameter. No additional constraints (e.g., authentication) are required beyond any gate check, which is not tied to the redirect value.
